The Integration Pitch

Built for person-centered care, not paperwork

At Grupo Hospitalario La Paz, delivering person-centered care means every clinician who touches a patient — from admissions to the specialist reviewing a chart hours later — needs the same complete picture. In most hospital groups, that picture is scattered: admissions data lives in one system, lab and imaging results in another, clinical notes in a third, and coordinating a single patient's journey means chasing down records instead of caring for the person in front of you.

Every minute a nurse or care coordinator spends re-entering data, calling another department for a result, or hunting down a referral is a minute not spent on the patient — the opposite of what a person-centered model is supposed to deliver. Vorro connects the systems already in place across a hospital group's clinical, diagnostic, and administrative core into one interoperable layer, using standards like FHIR, HL7, and C-CDA, so information follows the patient instead of staying trapped in a department.

On top of that connected record, Vorro's ambient documentation layer lets clinicians capture the visit conversation directly — automatically drafting notes, structured ICD-10/CPT coding, and a patient-friendly summary in real time, with live translation available for patients who don't speak Spanish. For a program built around putting the person at the center of care, that's time given back to the bedside, and a record that keeps up with the encounter instead of falling behind it.

Also from Vorro

Vorro can bring ambient AI into the room on the same connected layer: it listens with consent, writes the visit note and suggests the medical codes — landing in the hospital's clinical record system through the connectors Vorro already runs.
